newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 29.

text.p: NKK Corp plans to increase its crude steel production capacity at its Fukuyama plant in Hiroshima, southwest Japan, to 12 million tonnes per year by March 1999, to meet growing demand for crude steel in Asia.

Hinomaru Kotsu KK, a leading Tokyo-based taxi company, will apply to the Transport Ministry in February for permission to operate taxis with an initial charge of 100 yen for the first 250 meters. Hinomaru hopes to begin operating the taxis in Tokyo from April 1.

Nintendo Co Ltd plans to boost shipments of its Nintendo 64 video game machines from 700,000 to one million per month from April 1 on the back of brisk sales, particularly in the United States. It will also sell the game machines in Europe from March.

Three South Korean leading chip makers, including Samsung Electronics Co, plan to cut production of 16-megabit dynamic random-access memory chips (DRAMs) due to falling prices. They hope to increase the unit price to around $10 from $6. The move may affect capital investment at Japanese semiconductor makers in the fiscal year starting on April 1.

Aderans Co Ltd is expecting to report record current profit of 9.1 billion yen in the year ending in February, up 36 percent from the year before. This is due to profits from hair tonics and related products. But Aderans will see falling profits from its mainstay wig business.
